items.title: Hawkish Fed pivot under Warsh
items.detail: Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) called inflation 'too high' and put price stability first, spiking Sept rate-HIKE odds to ~57% and lifting the 10-yr to ~4.72% / 30-yr to ~5.21%. A higher-for-longer (or hiking) Fed de-rates long-duration equities.

items.title: Mega-cap AI priced for perfection
items.detail: NVDA beat big ($96.2B rev, $108B guide) yet fell -4.6% Friday - proof the group is priced for flawless execution. Any margin or demand blemish triggers outsized downside across the AI complex.

items.title: Memory-cost inflation squeezing AI-hardware margins
items.detail: NVDA guided gross margin down to 71-72% on rising memory costs. Good for memory makers (MU, SK Hynix), but a margin headwind for the broader AI-hardware chain if memory pricing keeps climbing.

items.title: AI-power / rate-sensitivity
items.detail: The 'AI electricity' basket (CEG, VST, GEV, CCJ) fell 2-6% on the yield spike - these long-duration infra names are the most fragile part of the market when rates rise.

items.title: Energy rollover
items.detail: Brent fell ~5% on the week to ~89.31 (WTI ~83.40) as Iran/Hormuz tensions eased - a headwind to energy earnings and sentiment after months of leadership.

items.title: Trade-policy escalation
items.detail: Canada announced 15-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods (metals tariffs doubling to 50%) starting Sept 8 - a fresh supply-chain/cost overhang for industrials and materials.

items.title: Volatility complacency
items.detail: VIX hit a year-low 14.35 into a hawkish catalyst - little hedging cushion in the market if an unexpected shock arrives.

items.title: Consumer softening
items.detail: July new-home sales -10.5%, weak consumer confidence, and Dick's Sporting Goods -30% on a guide cut hint the US consumer is cooling - a risk to discretionary names.
